chapters.title: Mangalacharana — Invocation and the Nature of Svara

verses.sanskrit: श्रीमच्छिवस्वरोदयं परमगुह्यं महेश्वरात् | प्राप्तं पार्वत्युवाचेदं सर्वलोकहितैषिणी ||
verses.transliteration: śrīmacchivasvarodayaṃ paramaguhyaṃ maheśvarāt | prāptaṃ pārvatyuvācedaṃ sarvalokahitaiṣiṇī ||
verses.translation: The auspicious Shiva Swarodaya — the supremely secret knowledge received from Maheshvara — Parvati, desiring the welfare of all worlds, declared thus.
verses.hindi: यह श्रीशिवस्वरोदय — महेश्वर से प्राप्त परम गुह्य ज्ञान — Parvati ने समस्त लोकों के हित की इच्छा से इस प्रकार कहा।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya's framing is distinctive: Parvati does not merely receive the teaching — she transmits it to all worlds out of compassion. The knowledge is "paramaguhyam" — supremely secret — not because it is esoteric but because it is radically simple and thus overlooked. The most universal, most available, most intimate phenomenon in human experience — the breath — is the vehicle of the highest knowledge. The text's revolutionary claim: you do not need to go anywhere, attain anything, or learn any complex system. The answer to every question about timing, health, and the quality of action is in your nostrils right now. The "secret" is that what you are looking for is the closest possible thing to you.

verses.sanskrit: स्वरज्ञो जीवति निश्चितं | स्वरविहीनो मृतः सदा ||
verses.transliteration: svarajño jīvati niścitaṃ | svaravihīno mṛtaḥ sadā ||
verses.translation: One who knows the svara truly lives. One devoid of svara-knowledge is as good as dead.
verses.hindi: स्वर जाननेवाला निश्चित रूप से जीता है। स्वर से विहीन व्यक्ति सदा मृत है।
verses.commentary: "Svarajño jīvati niścitaṃ" — the one who knows the svara truly lives. This is the Shiva Swarodaya's most concentrated statement: knowing the breath-science is not an addition to life, it is the condition of genuine life. "Svaravihīno mṛtaḥ sadā" — without svara-knowledge, one is perpetually dead. Not physically dead — but living unconsciously, reacting to circumstances without the fundamental self-knowledge that the breath provides. The svara is not just about the physical breath; it is about alignment — acting when the svara supports the action, resting when it supports rest, meditating when it supports stillness. To live without this alignment is to live mechanically, driven by habit and circumstance rather than by intelligent co-operation with one's own nature.

chapters.title: Tattva Viveka — Detecting the Active Element in the Breath

verses.sanskrit: पृथिव्यां स्थिरकार्याणि जले सर्वे शुभा क्रियाः | वह्नौ च क्रूरकर्माणि वायौ खेचरणं तथा | व्योम्नि नैव शुभं कार्यं सर्वसिद्धिस्तु शून्यके ||
verses.transliteration: pṛthivyāṃ sthirakāryāṇi jale sarve śubhā kriyāḥ | vahnau ca krūrakarmāṇi vāyau khecaraṇaṃ tathā | vyomni naiva śubhaṃ kāryaṃ sarvasiddhistu śūnyake ||
verses.translation: In earth: stable, enduring works. In water: all auspicious actions. In fire: fierce, forceful actions. In air: movement and travel. In ether: no ordinary task should be started — but all siddhi is in the void.
verses.hindi: पृथ्वी में: स्थिर और टिकाऊ कार्य। जल में: सभी शुभ कार्य। अग्नि में: कठोर और बलपूर्वक कार्य। वायु में: गति और यात्रा। आकाश में: कोई सांसारिक कार्य न करें — पर समस्त सिद्धि शून्य में है।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya's complete tattva-karma matrix — the matching of the active breath-element to the appropriate category of action. This is the most practically specific teaching in the text. Prithvi (earth) breath — long, slow, stable: optimal for laying foundations, starting businesses, building relationships, studying — anything requiring sustained effort over time. Jala (water) breath — cool, flowing, medium duration: optimal for all auspicious actions including ceremonies, new beginnings, important conversations, healing. Agni (fire) breath — fast, heating: optimal for physical combat, confrontation, surgery, cooking — anything requiring force. Vayu (air) breath — fast, mobile: for travel, quick tasks, physical movement. Akasha (ether) breath — subtle, barely perceptible: the Shiva Swarodaya says this is not suitable for ordinary action but is the supreme state for meditation and spiritual practice. "Sarvasiddhistu śūnyake" — all siddhi is in the void.

verses.sanskrit: यदा स्यात् सुषुम्नायां वहति मारुतः | तदा न शुभकार्याणि न च मोक्षस्य साधनम् || सुषुम्नायां भवेद्ध्यानं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā syāt suṣumnāyāṃ vahati mārutaḥ | tadā na śubhakāryāṇi na ca mokṣasya sādhanam || suṣumnāyāṃ bhavedhyānaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam ||
verses.translation: When the breath flows in Sushumna — neither for worldly auspicious tasks, nor even for ordinary moksha practice. In Sushumna, meditation becomes the giver of all siddhi.
verses.hindi: जब श्वास सुषुम्ना में बहती है — न शुभ सांसारिक कार्य के लिए, न साधारण मोक्ष-साधन के लिए। सुषुम्ना में ध्यान सर्वसिद्धि देने वाला हो जाता है।
verses.commentary: The supreme teaching on Sushumna. When both nostrils are equally open — the transitional moment between Ida and Pingala dominance — the Shiva Swarodaya says: do not use this for any worldly task, however auspicious. Do not even use it for ordinary spiritual practice. Use it only for meditation. "Suṣumnāyāṃ bhavedhyānaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam" — in Sushumna, meditation becomes the giver of all siddhi. Why? Because Sushumna is the moment of balance between the solar and lunar currents — the transitional state in which the ordinarily separate channels of activation and receptivity, effort and rest, are momentarily unified. The meditator who catches this moment and drops into stillness finds that the practice goes incomparably deeper than at any other time. The Shiva Swarodaya recommends checking for Sushumna at dawn, at dusk, and at the natural transition between nostrils throughout the day.

chapters.title: Svara Phala — Reading Events from the Breath

verses.sanskrit: प्रश्नकाले तु यो देही वहेत् स्वरेण संयुतः | तस्य कार्यं भवेत् सिद्धं सर्वेषामपि निश्चितम् ||
verses.transliteration: praśnakāle tu yo dehī vahet svareṇa saṃyutaḥ | tasya kāryaṃ bhavet siddhaṃ sarveṣāmapi niścitam ||
verses.translation: At the moment a question arises, the svara that flows in the questioner — by that svara, their work will succeed. This is certain for all.
verses.hindi: जिस क्षण प्रश्न उठे, उस समय जो स्वर बहता हो — उस स्वर से उस व्यक्ति का कार्य सिद्ध होगा। यह सभी के लिए निश्चित है।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya's method of svara-prashna (breath-based inquiry): at the moment a question or intention arises, note the dominant svara. If Ida (left nostril) is flowing: the outcome of contemplative, creative, relational, or inward-directed actions will be positive. If Pingala (right nostril) is flowing: the outcome of physical, analytical, assertive, or outward-directed actions will be positive. If Sushumna: the text gives mixed guidance — auspicious for spiritual intentions, uncertain for worldly ones. The underlying logic is not magic but physiology: the dominant svara reflects the current neurological state of the body-mind, and different states are genuinely more capable of different types of action. Reading the svara at the moment of an intention is reading the body's own readiness signal for that intention.

verses.sanskrit: यावज्जीवं प्राणवायुः स्वरेण वहति क्रमात् | तावत् स्वस्थः स्वस्थचित्तो जीवेत् सुखेन मानवः ||
verses.transliteration: yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇavāyuḥ svareṇa vahati kramāt | tāvat svasthaḥ svasthacitto jīvet sukhena mānaḥ ||
verses.translation: As long as the prana flows rhythmically in the svara cycle throughout life, the person remains healthy in body and mind, and lives happily.
verses.hindi: जब तक जीवन में प्राणवायु क्रमशः स्वर में बहती रहती है, तब तक मनुष्य स्वस्थ शरीर और चित्त से सुखपूर्वक जीता है।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya's health theorem: health is not the absence of disease but the regular, rhythmic alternation of the svara cycle throughout life. "Svareṇa vahati kramāt" — flowing in the svara cycle in order: the regular alternation of Ida and Pingala, with Sushumna arising naturally at the transitions, is the physiological definition of health in this text. Any disruption of this rhythm — one nostril remaining dominant for too long, the natural alternation becoming erratic — is the earliest signal of approaching disorder. The text provides specific patterns of disrupted svara that predict specific diseases, long before symptoms appear. This is the Shiva Swarodaya's most remarkable diagnostic claim: the breath cycle is the earliest diagnostic signal available, preceding clinical symptoms by days or weeks.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च स्वरे तिष्ठन्ति सर्वदा | स्वरेण गणिताः सर्वे स्वरे सूर्यः प्रतिष्ठितः ||
verses.transliteration: brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca svare tiṣṭhanti sarvadā | svareṇa gaṇitāḥ sarve svare sūryaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
verses.translation: Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra always dwell in the svara. All are enumerated through the svara. The sun itself is established in the svara.
verses.hindi: ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और रुद्र सदा स्वर में रहते हैं। सभी स्वर से ही गिने जाते हैं। स्वर में ही सूर्य प्रतिष्ठित है।
verses.commentary: The cosmic scope of the Shiva Swarodaya's claim: the three great functions of creation (Brahma), preservation (Vishnu), and dissolution (Rudra) are all contained within the svara. "Svare sūryaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ" — the sun itself is established in the svara. The breath is not a small biological event enclosed within the body — it is the meeting point of the individual and the cosmic, the place where the universal prana becomes personal and the personal prana reveals itself as universal. The text is making the same claim as the Chandogya Upanishad's Madhu Vidya in physiological language: the microcosm (individual breath) and macrocosm (cosmic breath/solar cycle) are structurally identical. To know one completely is to know the other.

verses.sanskrit: दक्षिणा नाड़ी सूर्यस्य वामा चन्द्रमस्य च | सुषुम्ना अग्नेः स्वरूपा त्रयो देवा महेश्वराः ||
verses.transliteration: dakṣiṇā nāḍī sūryasya vāmā candramasya ca | suṣumnā agneḥ svarūpā trayo devā maheśvarāḥ ||
verses.translation: The right nadi is of the sun, the left is of the moon. Sushumna is the form of fire — the three are the great gods.
verses.hindi: दाहिनी नाड़ी सूर्य की है, बायीं चंद्रमा की। सुषुम्ना अग्नि का स्वरूप है — ये तीन महादेव हैं।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya identifies the three nadis with cosmic principles: Pingala (right) with the sun, Ida (left) with the moon, and Sushumna (central) with fire (Agni). These three are not merely physiological channels but the three great gods (Maheshvaras) in the body. The sun is active, outward, heating; the moon is receptive, inward, cooling; fire is transformative, central. The practice of svara yoga is the harmonisation of these three principles.

verses.sanskrit: स्वरोदये शिवः साक्षात् प्राणे विष्णुरुद्यतः | रक्ते ब्रह्मा स्थितो नित्यं त्रयो देवाः प्रकाशिताः ||
verses.transliteration: svarodaye śivaḥ sākṣāt prāṇe viṣṇurudyataḥ | rakte brahmā sthito nityaṃ trayo devāḥ prakāśitāḥ ||
verses.translation: In the breath is Shiva directly; in the prana is Vishnu ever-moving. In the blood is Brahma eternally — the three gods are revealed.
verses.hindi: साँस में शिव साक्षात हैं; प्राण में विष्णु सदैव चल रहे हैं। रक्त में ब्रह्मा नित्य स्थित हैं — तीनों देव प्रकट हैं।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya locates the trinity within the body: Shiva in the breath (svara), Vishnu in the prana (vital force), and Brahma in the blood (rakta). This is not metaphor but recognition: the breath is the witness (Shiva), the prana is the sustaining force (Vishnu), and the blood is the creative flow (Brahma). The body itself is the temple of the gods. Svara yoga is the practice of recognising these divine presences within.

verses.translation: Purification of the nadis is the foundation of yoga; liberation comes from nadi purification. Establishing the body is yoga; knowledge of nadis is supreme.
verses.hindi: नाड़ीयों की शुद्धि योग की नींव है; मुक्ति नाड़ीशुद्धि से आती है। शरीर की स्थापना योग है; नाड़ीविज्ञान उत्तम है।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya declares that nadi purification is the foundation of yoga and the cause of liberation. This is a radical claim: not meditation, not asana, not mantra — but the purification of the subtle energy channels. When the nadis are clear, prana flows freely through Sushumna, and the Self recognises itself. The body is established in yoga when the nadis are balanced. Knowledge of the nadis is the supreme knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चतत्त्वानि पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चप्राणाः पञ्चभूतानि | सर्वं शिवस्य स्वरूपं यो वेद स पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: pañcatattvāni pañcendriyāṇi pañcaprāṇāḥ pañcabhūtāni | sarvaṃ śivasya svarūpaṃ yo veda sa paśyati ||
verses.translation: The five elements, the five senses, the five pranas, the five beings — all are the form of Shiva. He who knows, sees.
verses.hindi: पाँच तत्त्व, पाँच इंद्रियाँ, पाँच प्राण, पाँच भूत — सब शिव का स्वरूप हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है।
verses.commentary: The Shiva Swarodaya culminates in a declaration of non-duality: everything — the five elements, the five senses, the five pranas, the five beings — is the form of Shiva. This is not pantheism but recognition: the apparent multiplicity of existence is all one reality appearing in many forms. The one who knows this sees the form of Shiva in everything. The practice of svara yoga leads to this recognition.
